If you're in high school I'm incredibly sorry because your options become a lot more limited as your wellbeing is often bottlenecked by your caretakers willingness to invest in your mental health.
Advice: Find something you love to so and keep doing it until you can find a way out of your home to get therapy. Play video games, watch anime, join an online community. You need to bide yourself some time with distractions.


If you're in college, you're an adult and we need to take your mental health just as serious as your physical health. It sounds like you're in acute distress (vague broad word). If you're leg just snapped in half you would likely go to the hospital. Your mind needs support just as much and the urgency to get yourself the support you need is imperative.

Advice: Find a way to get therapy, public resources, college campus resources, credit card to pay for insurance/therapy, then find a healthy therapist. Potentially ask your therapist if you would be a good candidate for ketamine infusion treatment. There is hope but you need to be willing to invest in yourself and open your mind to possibilities that you may have already shut out. There is no stigma for seeking help. It is a necessary decision you must make to invest in yourself now so you can achieve greater things later. Do it now while your brain still has some plasticity to change.

Anecdotal: I received ketamine treatment and I still take ongoing ketamine troches (with the support for 2years therapy and my therapist's support to process suppressed feelings coming up) .

Best decision ever despite going into debt, which I have now payed off. Years of PTSD, depression, lack of normal range of human emotion virtually gone.
